title: MCTS, Bandits, and AlphaZero: Planning and Exploration in RL
description: A comprehensive collection on Monte Carlo Tree Search, multi-armed bandits with UCB algorithms, and their application in AlphaZero-style reinforcement learning systems.

sections.title: Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS)
sections.notes: Core MCTS theory and practical implementations, including generalizations to stochastic environments and graph structures.

papers.notes: Interesting generalisation to loops (where nodes are visited several times in a rollout) and asymmetric trees. Sets unvisited child node count to infinity—similar to some GitHub implementations. This approach will at first always explore all child nodes once, but this becomes difficult if each node has many child nodes, as the number of nodes to explore explodes exponentially. Similar to standard UCB where all nodes are first explored once.
Generalisation to stochastic move outcomes using FrozenLake environment. Also links to related works.
Interesting intro to UTC and PUCT. Extension to algorithm.
Thesis on adding planning model to PUCT. AlphaZero/AlphaGo focused. Intro to MCTS, UCT, PUCT and more.

sections.title: Upper Confidence Bound (UCB) Algorithms
sections.notes: Theoretical foundations and practical applications of UCB for multi-armed bandits, contextual bandits, and neural network extensions.

papers.notes: Good explanation and derivation for (sub) Gaussian noise. Includes proof of regret bound.
Detailed treatment. Only Bernoulli (but that also applies to sub-Gaussian, right?). Also includes a proof.
Extension to contextual bandits. But noise is still independent of context.
Referenced in NeuralUCB. Relies on oracle.
Gaussian, general, sub-Gaussian etc. and how they link up. These are used in UCB bounds.
